records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Subscription revenue increased by $48.5 million and $91.8 million during the three and six months ended January 31, 2025, respectively, compared to the same periods a year ago, primarily due to the impact of cloud transition agreements, new subscription agreements entered into and provisioned, and the renewal or extension of subscription services at the fully ramped annual fees after the initial committed term since January 31, 2024.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: We have experienced seasonal variations in our license revenue and, to a lesser extent, in our subscription revenue as a result of increased customer orders in our fourth fiscal quarter, which is the quarter ending July 31.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: The success of our sales efforts relies on continued improvements and enhancements to our current products, the introduction of new products, efficient and secure operation of our cloud infrastructure, continued development of relevant local content and automated tools for updating content, and successful implementations and migrations.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Because we pay our services professionals the same amount throughout the year, our gross margins on our services revenue are usually lower in these quarters.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Our net cash provided by (used in) operating activities is significantly impacted by the timing of invoicing and collections of accounts receivable, the timing and amount of annual bonus payments, as well as payroll, commissions, payroll taxes, and other tax payments.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Revenue: For fiscal 2025, revenue was $37.9 billion, an increase of nine percent year-over-year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The increase in subscription and support revenues for fiscal 2025 was primarily caused by volume-driven increases from new business, which includes new customers, upgrades and additional subscriptions from existing customers.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Remaining Performance Obligation: Total remaining performance obligation, which represents all future revenue under contract yet to be recognized, as of January 31, 2025 was approximately $63.4 billion, an increase of 11 percent year-over-year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: For fiscal 2025, the increase in cost of revenues in absolute dollars was primarily due to an increase in employee-related costs, including stock-based compensation expense, partially offset by a decrease in amortization of purchased intangibles and a decrease in service delivery expenses.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Income from Operations: For fiscal 2025, income from operations was $7.2 billion as compared to $5.0 billion from a year ago.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Net sales in fiscal 2025 increased by 7.7% to $5.55 billion, from $5.15 billion in fiscal 2024.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Comparable retail store net sales increased as a result of higher store traffic and transactions, which were partially offset by a decrease in units per transaction.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Inventory as of January 31, 2025 and 2024 totaled $621.1 million and $550.2 million, representing 13.7% and 13.4% of total assets, respectively.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The deleverage in selling, general and administrative expenses as a rate to sales was primarily related to increased marketing expenses to support customer growth and increased sales in the Retail and Subscription segments.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Income from operations for fiscal 2025 was 8.5% of net sales, or $473.8 million, compared to 7.2% of net sales, or $369.8 million, for fiscal 2024.
